limits: No experiments, benchmarks or measured accuracy: every technique is shown with a single illustrative query.
Code uses older APIs (get_relevant_documents, langchain_core.pydantic_v1, gpt-3.5-turbo) that have since been deprecated (inferred from today's date).
Authors concede the security list for text-to-SQL is not exhaustive.
Indexing optimization (embedding, text splitting) is posed as a question in the chapter but not answered here.
practices: Keep k low; more documents cost latency, tokens and hallucination risk (retrieval section).
Rewrite poorly worded queries with an LLM before retrieval (Rewrite-Retrieve-Read), accepting an extra LLM call.
Use multi-query retrieval with deduplication by content when one query covers multiple perspectives.
Use RAG-Fusion (reciprocal rank fusion, k=60) to merge ranked lists from several queries.
Use HyDE: embed an LLM-written hypothetical passage instead of the raw query.
Use logical routing (function-calling schema) when data sources are a defined list; use semantic routing (embed prompts, cosine similarity) to pick a prompt.
Match LLM output leniently (lowercase, substring) for resilience to off-script output.
Implement each technique as a standalone chain so techniques can be combined.
Give the LLM CREATE TABLE descriptions, a few sample rows and few-shot question-query examples for text-to-SQL.
Run LLM-generated SQL with a read-only user, access to only needed tables and a time-out.

creating a hypothetical document based on the user's query, embedding the document, and retrieving relevant documents based on vector similarity
